original_question: Is there any semigroup conjugacy relation that is not partition-covering, meaning that there exists some partition of some set that cannot be realized as the conjugacy classes of a semigroup for that relation?
target_in_paper: Section 4 ("Non-Partition Covering Conjugacies"), opening unnumbered question asking whether there are any semigroup conjugacies that are not partition-covering. The paper immediately answers this in the affirmative. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2411.16284))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right existential issue and correctly paraphrases failure of partition-covering as the existence of a set together with a partition that cannot arise as the conjugacy classes of any semigroup for the chosen relation. That is exactly the question raised at the start of Section 4. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2411.16284))
missing_details: The paper uses "semigroup conjugacy" in a technical sense: it is an equivalence relation that agrees with ordinary group conjugacy whenever the semigroup is actually a group. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2411.16284))

To be fully stand-alone, the positive definition of partition-covering should be stated explicitly: for every set X and every partition P of X, there exists a semigroup S with underlying set X such that the conjugacy classes of S under the relation are exactly the blocks of P. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2411.16284))

The intended scope is existence of some semigroup conjugacy failing partition-covering, not a question about the six standard relations treated in Theorem 3.3, because the paper has already proved those six are partition-covering. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2411.16284))

The nearest paper-faithful target is this general existence question from Section 4, not the later narrower question in the same section about whether a particular relation is the smallest conjugacy that is not partition-covering. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2411.16284))
refined_question: Does there exist a semigroup conjugacy relation ~—that is, an equivalence relation on semigroups which coincides with ordinary group conjugacy whenever the semigroup is a group—that is not partition-covering, in the sense that there exist a set X and a partition P of X for which no semigroup S with underlying set X has its ~-conjugacy classes exactly equal to the blocks of P? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2411.16284))
justification: The draft is aiming at the opening question of Section 4, where the paper asks whether any semigroup conjugacies fail to be partition-covering. The introduction supplies the precise definitions of both "semigroup conjugacy" and "partition-covering," while Theorem 3.3 explains the local context by showing that six standard conjugacies are partition-covering before Section 4 turns to counterexamples. So the sharpest stand-alone rewrite is the general existence question above, and it should not be broadened into a classification problem or redirected to a different open problem. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2411.16284))
